finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the `target` query parameter straight to http.Get with no validation. An attacker can make the server request any URL, including internal services and cloud metadata such as http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/. The response body is copied back to the caller, so this is full-read SSRF. Error text is also reflected.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the response streamed to the client via io.Copy at main.go:22

trace.note: /fetch is registered to the fetch handler, with no auth or middleware
target is read from the query string
target is passed unvalidated to http.Get, which follows redirects and uses the default client
The upstream response body is written back to the attacker

finding.guards_checked: There is no scheme check, host allowlist, IP or private-range check, or egress filtering in this code. The `allowed` map is used only by safeFetch, not by fetch. There is no authentication on the route. Go's http.Get only supports http and https, so file:// and gopher:// are not reachable. This does not limit access to internal HTTP services.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 pass the unauthenticated `target` query param directly to http.Get with no validation, and main.go:22 copies the body back. The `allowed` host check exists only in safeFetch (main.go:27), and /fetch is registered at main.go:41 with no middleware.
